raw.title: Instant Pot HK Onion Pork Chops
equipment: Instant Pot or electric pressure cooker
raw.notes: Converted from US tablespoons and inches. Stock kept at the source's own metric figure (188 ml). Cornflour (cornstarch) given as about 12 g for 1 1/2 US tbsp. Kosher salt: any cooking salt works, go lighter if it's fine-grained. Source tested 1 min high pressure + full natural release as the best result across 5 batches; chops with some fat marbling work best.

ingredients.name: boneless pork chops
ingredients.note: about 3 cm thick, ideally with some fat marbling

steps.title: Tenderise the chops
steps.text: Pound both sides of each pork chop hard with the back of a heavy knife or a meat tenderiser, in a criss-cross pattern.
steps.tip: Don't hold back – chops handle the force, and it breaks up the fibres just enough.

steps.title: Marinate the chops
steps.text: Coat the chops with 15 ml soy sauce, 15 ml Shaoxing wine, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp sugar, 1/4 tsp white pepper and 1/4 tsp sesame oil.
steps.tip: Slice the onion and measure out the sauce ingredients while this runs.

steps.title: Heat the pot
steps.text: Press Sauté and let the pot get as hot as it can before the chops go in, so they don't stick.

steps.title: Brown the chops
steps.text: Add 15 ml olive oil and spread it over the whole base. Brown the chops on each side without flipping constantly, then set aside, keeping the juices.
steps.cue: Browned but not burnt, about 1–1.5 minutes per side.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Add 120 g sliced onion, with a pinch of kosher salt and black pepper if you like, and cook.

steps.title: Deglaze with balsamic
steps.text: Add 15 ml balsamic vinegar and scrape up part of the browned bits from the base with a wooden spoon.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Add 188 ml chicken stock, 15 ml Worcestershire, 15 ml soy sauce and 1 tsp sugar. Mix and fully deglaze. Taste and add kosher salt if needed.

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Return the chops and all their juices to the pot. Lock the lid and cook at High Pressure for 1 minute.

steps.title: Natural release
steps.text: When the cook time ends, let the pressure release fully on its own – don't vent.

steps.title: Season the sauce
steps.text: Lift out the chops and set aside. Press Sauté on medium, taste the sauce and add more salt if you like.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Mix 12 g cornflour with 30 ml water. Stir it into the sauce a third at a time until it's as thick as you want.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the onion sauce over the chops and serve straight away.

raw.title: Coffee jelly (espresso, gelatine)
raw.notes: Adapted for espresso and gelatine. Coffee: 600 ml strong-brewed coffee replaced with 6 single shots (~180 ml) plus 420 ml water; for a bolder jelly use 8 shots (~240 ml) and 360 ml water. Setting agent: 4 g kanten replaced with 8 g powdered gelatine, the source's soft-set substitute. Gelatine gives a soft, wobbly jelly too soft to cube, so it's set and served in individual glasses and eaten with a spoon. Use more gelatine for a firmer set (one reader used 12 g). Brands vary, so check your packet's blooming instructions, and never boil gelatine or it won't set. Chilling adds 4–5 hours. Tablespoons converted to ml. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 60 ml cold for blooming, 360 ml heated

ingredients.name: powdered gelatine
ingredients.original: 4 g kanten powder (substitute 8 g powdered gelatin)

ingredients.name: whipped cream, coffee beans, mint leaves

steps.title: Pull the shots
steps.text: Pull 6 single shots of espresso (about 180 ml) into a jug and set aside.

steps.title: Bloom the gelatine
steps.text: Sprinkle 8 g gelatine over 60 ml cold water in a small bowl and leave it to bloom.
steps.tip: Check your packet for blooming time — brands vary.

steps.title: Heat water and sugar
steps.text: Warm 360 ml water and 75 g sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
steps.cue: Hot and steaming but not boiling — boiled gelatine won't set.

steps.title: Dissolve the gelatine
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat. Whisk in the bloomed gelatine until fully dissolved, then whisk in the 180 ml espresso.

steps.title: Pour into glasses
steps.text: Let the mixture cool for 5 minutes, then pour it into 4 glass serving dishes.
steps.tip: Gelatine jelly is too soft to cube, so it sets and is served in the glasses.

steps.title: Pop the bubbles
steps.text: Quickly touch the surface bubbles with a kitchen torch or long lighter flame, or scoop them off with a spoon.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.text: Let the glasses cool to room temperature on the bench. Cover with a paper towel and plastic wrap, then refrigerate.
steps.tip: The paper towel soaks up condensation.

steps.title: Mix the topping
steps.text: Stir 45 ml sweetened condensed milk with 45 ml milk. Add more condensed milk for a sweeter, thicker drizzle.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Top each glass with whipped cream, a coffee bean and mint, then drizzle with the condensed milk topping. Eat with a spoon.

raw.title: Pressure Cooker Japanese Curry
equipment: Instant Pot (6 qt) or stovetop pressure cooker
raw.notes: Converted from US lb, cups and tablespoons; onion, carrot and potato weights are the source's own metric figures. Times allow about 20 min for the pot to come up to pressure; natural release (about 15 min) isn't included in the total. Curry roux: check the weight — you need 200–230 g, and some boxes are smaller, so you may need two. The author mixes half mild and half medium-hot roux. Homemade roux: solid cubes go on top before cooking like store-bought; freshly made (non-solid) roux goes in after pressure cooking — sauté 5 min until blended, then season. Stovetop pressure cooker: lock the lid, set to high pressure, heat over medium-high until it reaches high pressure, then turn to medium-low to hold it and cook 15 min. Substitutions: pork or beef chuck roast instead of chicken (not beef stew meat — it won't get tender). For lower sodium use water, or half stock and half water. Don't use russet potatoes; cut the veg slightly bigger if you want to avoid a mushy texture. Storage: fridge up to 3 days, freezer 1 month (remove potatoes before freezing; thaw in the fridge for 24 hours). Reheat gently on low with 120 ml water or more stirred in so the thickened sauce doesn't burn.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.note: half the amount for table salt; plus more to taste

steps.title: Soak the potatoes
steps.text: Peel 432 g Yukon gold potatoes, cut them into quarters and soak in water to remove the excess starch.
steps.tip: Moved first so the soak is done by the time the pot is ready. Have your rice cooked or cooking too.

steps.title: Cut the onions
steps.text: Cut 1005 g yellow onions (3 large) in half, then cut each half into 5 wedges.

steps.title: Cut the carrots
steps.text: Peel 143 g carrots (1½) and cut into bite-sized pieces, rangiri-style (roll-cut on an angle).
steps.tip: Rangiri adds surface area so the carrots absorb flavour and cook faster.

steps.title: Garlic and ginger
steps.text: Mince 2 garlic cloves. Grate the ginger and reserve 1 tsp, with its juice.

steps.title: Cut and season chicken
steps.text: Cut 680 g chicken thighs into flat, bite-sized pieces (sogigiri, slicing at an angle). Season with ⅛ tsp kosher salt and ⅛ tsp black pepper.

steps.title: Heat the pot
steps.text: Press Sauté on the Instant Pot. When the inner pot is hot, add 15 ml neutral oil and spread it evenly.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.text: Add the onion wedges, minced garlic and grated ginger with juice, and quickly mix well.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken pieces and mix until just coated with the oil.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Drain the potatoes. Add the carrots and potatoes to the pot and mix well.

steps.title: Add stock and roux
steps.text: Pour in 720 ml chicken stock and press the meat and veg down into the liquid. Place 200 g curry roux cubes on top. Do not mix.
steps.tip: If mixed in, the roux can sink and burn on the bottom.

steps.title: Seal and come to pressure
steps.text: Lock the lid with the valve on Sealing. Press Keep Warm/Cancel, then Meat/Stew, and set the time to 15 minutes. Wait for it to come up to pressure.
steps.tip: The 15-minute countdown on the pot only starts once it's at pressure.

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Pressure cook for 15 minutes. The pot switches to Keep Warm when done.

steps.title: Release the pressure
steps.text: Slide the handle to Venting until the float valve drops, or let the pressure release naturally.
steps.tip: Natural release takes about 15 minutes; skip the timer if venting.

steps.title: Unlock and taste
steps.text: Carefully unlock the lid, watching for hot steam. Taste the sauce and add kosher salt to your liking.
steps.tip: The author suggests 2–4 tsp Diamond Crystal salt, depending on your stock and roux.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Add 15 ml ketchup and 15 ml soy sauce. Stir well to dissolve the roux.

steps.title: Serve over rice
steps.text: Portion 6 servings of rice onto plates and spoon the curry on top. Add fukujinzuke on the side if you like.

raw.title: Pressure Cooker Beef and Vegetable Stew
equipment: Rimmed baking sheet or large plate
raw.notes: Amounts use the recipe's own metric figures; US tablespoons of liquid are given in ml. The source lists the beef as 3 lb (1.25 kg), but 3 lb is closer to 1.36 kg, so anything from 1.25 to 1.4 kg of chuck works. Instead of the anchovies you can use 15 ml Asian fish sauce. The wine can be dry sherry, dry vermouth or red wine. Several reviewers found the stated pressure times too long and cut them to about 18 minutes for the beef and 4 minutes after the potatoes go in; the cards keep the recipe's 30 and 15 minutes. The stew keeps for up to 5 days in the fridge and reheats well.

ingredients.name: anchovy fillets
ingredients.original: 3 oil- or salt-packed anchovy fillets, rinsed (or 1 tablespoon/15ml Asian fish sauce)
ingredients.note: oil- or salt-packed, rinsed; or 15 ml fish sauce

ingredients.name: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
medium carrots
ingredients.note: 2 left whole, 2 cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.name: dry sherry, dry vermouth or red wine

steps.title: Blend the broth base
steps.text: Blend 720 ml stock, 30 g gelatine, 75 g tomato paste, 15 ml soy sauce, 3 anchovy fillets and 15 ml Worcestershire on high speed. Set aside.
steps.tip: If your pearl onions are frozen, set them out to thaw now. They go in at the mushroom stage.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat 30 ml oil in the pressure cooker over medium-high until shimmering. Season the 3 chuck steaks all over with salt and pepper, then brown in a single layer, turning occasionally.
steps.tip: Work in batches if the steaks don't fit in one layer.

steps.title: Set the beef aside
steps.text: Transfer the browned steaks to a rimmed baking sheet or large plate and set aside. Keep any juices that collect.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Add 280 g quartered mushrooms to the cooker and cook, stirring, lowering the heat as needed to stop them scorching.
steps.cue: Liquid released and mushrooms starting to brown.

steps.title: Brown carrots and onions
steps.text: Add the 2 chopped carrots and 225 g pearl onions and cook, stirring, a few minutes longer. Season with salt and pepper, then transfer to a bowl and set aside.

steps.title: Brown the aromatics
steps.text: Add the halved onion cut side down, plus the 2 whole carrots, 2 celery sticks and 3 unpeeled garlic cloves. Cook, turning the carrots, celery and garlic occasionally.

steps.title: Deglaze and add broth
steps.text: Add 235 ml sherry or wine, scrape up the browned bits with a wooden spoon and reduce. Then pour in the blended broth base.

steps.title: Cut and flour the beef
steps.text: Cut the seared steaks into 4–5 cm chunks, put them in a large bowl and toss with 20 g flour.

steps.title: Seal and pressurise
steps.text: Add the beef and any tray juices to the cooker with 2 bay leaves and 4 thyme sprigs. Stir, seal and bring to high pressure.

steps.title: Pressure cook the beef
steps.text: Cook at high pressure, then rapidly release the pressure and open the cooker.
steps.tip: Start the timer once the cooker reaches high pressure.

steps.title: Remove the aromatics
steps.text: With tongs, fish out and discard the whole carrots, celery, thyme, bay leaves, onion and garlic.

steps.title: Add potatoes and vegetables
steps.text: Add 450 g cubed potatoes and the reserved mushrooms, pearl onions and carrots. Reseal and bring back to high pressure.

steps.title: Finish pressure cooking
steps.text: Cook at high pressure, then rapidly release the pressure.

steps.title: Add peas and serve
steps.text: Stir in 100 g frozen peas and season with salt and pepper if needed. Serve straight away.
steps.tip: Or cool and refrigerate for up to 5 days, then reheat to serve.

raw.title: Colombian chicken stew with potatoes, tomato and onion
raw.notes: Your tweaks, all from reader reviews on the page: one large carrot added and one potato dropped (Jonathan Hodge), two smashed garlic cloves in the pot (same review), a seasoning step for the chicken and vegetables (he used Goya Adobo; salt and pepper works too), and pressure time cut from 25 to 15 minutes (Kenji says 15 is enough in his YouTube video). Adobo is salty, so if you use it go lighter on the pinch of salt in the pot and adjust at the end. Converted 4 lb chicken to grams and inches to cm.

ingredients.name: large Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 2.5–5 cm chunks; one fewer than the original

ingredients.name: whole chicken, back removed, cut into 8 pieces (or 4 chicken legs, split into thighs and drumsticks)

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Season the 8 chicken pieces all over with adobo seasoning, or salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Do this a few hours ahead and refrigerate if you can, so the seasoning gets into the meat.

steps.title: Prep the vegetables
steps.text: Peel 3 potatoes and cut into 2.5–5 cm chunks. Slice the carrot into rounds and the onion 5 mm thick. Cut 4 tomatoes into chunks. Smash 2 garlic cloves.

steps.title: Season the vegetables
steps.text: Toss the potatoes, carrot, onion and tomatoes with a little adobo seasoning, or salt and pepper, just before cooking.

steps.title: Load the pressure cooker
steps.text: Put the vegetables, garlic, chicken and 2 bay leaves in the pressure cooker with a large pinch of salt. Toss with your hands to combine.
steps.tip: Go lighter on the salt if you seasoned with adobo.

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Seal the lid and cook under high pressure.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Release the pressure and remove the lid. Season to taste with salt and pepper, and serve.
